g.text: aq watches every Claude Code session in your tmux and puts
whatever needs you in one queue, shown one card at a time:
a diff to review, an edit to allow, a permission prompt.
This tour takes about four minutes, and most of it is you
pressing the keys on made-up cards.
skip the tour (F2 brings it back)
❯ the API's rate limit is one shared window; make it a token bucket per key
aq watches every Claude Code session in your tmux and puts
whatever needs you in one queue, shown one card at a time:
This tour takes about four minutes, and most of it is you
aq hears from Claude through three hooks in
~/.claude/settings.json; the README shows how to add them,
or has a prompt you can paste to Claude to do it for you.
Sessions started before the hooks were added need a restart.
Without aq running, the hooks do nothing at all.
The top bar counts what is waiting behind the card on screen.
Decide on a card and the next one comes up. A new card waits
its turn: it never takes the screen from the one you are on.
move, as in vim (also Ctrl-d, Ctrl-u, gg, G)
A card answered in its own window stays, marked "answered
elsewhere", and the next key only closes it. A card whose edit
changes under you ignores deciding keys for 1.5 s.
Next comes a practice review card, made up for this tour.
It is what you get when a session finishes a turn.
The tour tells you which key to press, one at a time.
Nothing you do on it reaches a real session.
leave the tour, during the practice too
to move down a line (k moves up)
to go to the next file (H goes back)
to switch between the split and unified views
to list every key that works here
│ aq collects what your Claude sessions in tmux need from you and shows it
│ one card at a time. The top bar counts what is waiting behind the card.
│ Each project (git checkout) has one mode, shown on its tab when it is not
│ review. M on a card from that project, or on its tab when nothing waits,
│ moves it to the next mode. A new mode applies from the session's next
│ finished turn; the card on screen stays as it is.
│ review board when a session finishes, review its whole diff and
│ send line comments back as one message
│ step by step each edit waits for you before it is applied; needs
│ the aq hooks, so restart sessions started before them
│ vibe nothing is checked: no cards when a session finishes
│ quiz when a session finishes, explain pieces of its diff in
│ your own words: what the code does, or why it was done
│ that way; one question on the whole change comes last.
│ A gap the judge finds becomes keep-as-is or send-a-fix
│ ? ask the agent a side question Space skip this card
│ W where are we: a short summary of what is done and what is left
│ N a new Claude session in this project, in a tmux window of its own;
│ what you type is its first prompt, and Tab gives it a git worktree
to comment on the line under the cursor
to save it, once you have typed a few words
to mark this file done: it is ticked and skipped from now on
to send your comments to the session as one message
to approve the change, which closes the card
That was review mode, the default. Each project (git
checkout) has its own mode, and M moves it to the next.
In step mode every edit waits for you before it is applied.
You let it through, or send it back with a reason.
move the practice project to step mode
Practice: approved, and the card is gone
to let this edit through; Claude is waiting on you
Raise when no name is given
to refuse this one: raising an error is not what you asked for
to send Claude your reason, once you have typed it
In quiz mode, when a session finishes, aq picks the parts of
the change that matter and asks you to explain them in your
own words. A judge marks each answer, and a gap it finds in
the code can go back to Claude as a fix.
In the practice the verdict is made up.
move the practice project to quiz mode
Practice: Claude would read your reason and try again
What does greet return for a name made only of spaces?
to answer the question in your own words
Practice: Claude would read your reason and try again
What does greet return for a name made only of spaces?
to hand in your answer, once you have typed it
'Hello, ' with no name: the check let
'Hello, ' with no name: the check lets
'Hello, ' with no name: the check lets spa
'Hello, ' with no name: the check lets space
'Hello, ' with no name: the check lets spaces t
'Hello, ' with no name: the check lets spaces thro
'Hello, ' with no name: the check lets spaces throug
'Hello, ' with no name: the check lets spaces through
The tour marks any answer right; a real judge reads yours. It also found a gap in the code: a name of only spaces
gets past the `not name` check, so greet returns 'Hello, ' with no name after it.
to have Claude fix the gap the judge found (y keeps the code)
when a session finishes, review its diff
every edit waits for you before it is applied
explain parts of the change in your own words
move the project to the next mode
A script can run in vibe while a payments service sits in
step: the mode is kept per project.
Practice: Claude would be asked to fix it

to pick the next session, web (h goes back)

Do the chart colours as we
to ask web where it is up to, without interrupting it

Left: dark colours for the charts.
(Made up for the tour. A real answer comes from a copy of the session, so the session itself
to jump to web's tmux window
to start another Claude session in web's project
╭ New Claude session in web (empty starts it bare) ────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
to start it (typed text is its first prompt, Tab adds a worktree)
╭ New Claude session in a new worktree of web (empty starts it bare) ──────────────────────────────╮
to move web's project on from quiz mode: watch its tab
once more, and it is back in review, the default
W and N work on a card too, for the card's session. So do:
ask the session a side question; a copy answers
a shell in a popup, with Claude's last ! command typed in
select text; letting go copies it
copy the word; a third click copies the line
That's it. F2 shows this tour again.
